clue.text: Mean there can't possibly be a race?

definitions.text: there can't possibly be a race?

explanation.surface: A sour remark that no contest can be held.
explanation.walkthrough: A small, poor place is a 'one-horse town', hence 'mean'; a race with a single runner is no race at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Petty and second-rate, as in a dull little town, and also describing a contest with only a single runner entered.

clue.text: Treading awkwardly-must be the slope ofthe hill

indicators.note: done awkwardly, the letters of the word before are clumsily rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone walking clumsily blames the steepness of the hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradient is the measure of how steeply ground rises, so it names a hill's incline.

clue.text: Get together for a photograph

explanation.surface: An invitation to gather for a group picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw nearer each other is to move in tight; a shot taken from very near the subject has the same name.

clue.text: Assert that it is earth surrounded by water

definitions.text: Assert that it is earth surrounded by water

parts.words: Assert that it is earth surrounded by water
parts.note: to assert that a thing is earth is to say it '...', and land with water on every side is the real meaning

explanation.surface: A geography lesson insisting that a piece of ground lies amid the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground with sea all round it is the dictionary sense, and the phrase 'is land' is the claim made in the clue.

clue.text: Security service organised raid above ground

parts.note: MI stands for Military Intelligence, as in MI5, Britain's security service

indicators.note: organised means the letters of the word beside it are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Spies plan a raid conducted from the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in flight, off the earth and not yet landed, is aloft.

clue.text: Manoeuvring single armies has nothing to compare with his military power

definitions.text: Manoeuvring single armies has nothing to compare with his military power

indicators.note: manoeuvring troops moves them about, so the letters of the following words are moved into a new order

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A supreme commander who moves whole armies about singlehandedly has no rival in might.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the supreme commander whose power is unmatched, while also giving the anagram plus O.
explanation.definitionFit: The title is given to a supreme commander over several armies, whose authority is unrivalled.

clue.text: Social gatherings voted for by horticulturalists

explanation.surface: Gardeners choosing which events to hold.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'parties' as political parties: the ones gardeners would elect.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdoor receptions held on lawns, and also, punningly, political groups that keen gardeners would support at the polls.

clue.text: Dole pains gone! Spell that out in Social Security terms

definitions.text: Dole pains gone! Spell that out in Social Security terms

indicators.note: to spell something out anew is to lay out its letters differently, signalling a rearrangement of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A pensioner rejoices that the hardship of the dole is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue gives both the rearranged fodder and the benefit that replaces dole for the retired.
explanation.definitionFit: A state payment to retired people, which ends reliance on unemployment benefit (British 'dole').

clue.text: Otherwise rebuked for a gorgeous bloomer

parts.note: or introduces the alternative, meaning otherwise
chid is an old past tense of chide, to rebuke

explanation.surface: A dressing-down for a blunder, or else a compliment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder; here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A showy tropical flower prized for its blooms.

clue.text: Leaving sheltered bays to, we hear, see sick bays?

indicators.note: we hear says a word is taken for its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: the clue word see is pronounced the same as the spelling entered
wards are hospital rooms, places where the sick lie

explanation.surface: A ship leaves the calm harbour, and someone visits the infirmary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. Heading out of the bays means going toward open water.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving toward open water, away from harbours and coves on land.

clue.text: Water that is about 100 degrees below boiling point

definitions.text: Water that is about 100 degrees below boiling point

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the abbreviation goes round the numeral

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of Latin id est, that is
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A science fact about frozen water's temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: In Celsius, water freezes at 0 and boils at 100, so frozen water is 100 degrees below boiling.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen water, solid at zero Celsius, a hundred degrees under the point at which water boils.

clue.text: Perceives the sound of a note preceding the funeral procession

parts.note: to perceive the sound of something is to hear it
E is one of the musical notes

explanation.surface: Someone hears a musical note just before a cortege passes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preceding' is a link: the vehicle carrying the coffin leads the cortege.
explanation.definitionFit: The vehicle bearing the coffin heads a cortege and stands for it here.

clue.text: Dungaree crumpled usually by them

indicators.note: crumpled clothing is pushed out of shape, so the letters of the garment are rearranged

explanation.surface: Children are the ones who usually leave overalls creased.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue says young people too young to be adults are the usual crumplers of dungarees.
explanation.definitionFit: Below the legal adult threshold, as children and teenagers who wear dungarees are.

clue.text: Brew tea and have tiffin

indicators.note: to brew is to mix and stew, so the letters of the word are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Make a pot of tea and take a light meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiffin is an Anglo-Indian word for a light lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a light midday meal means consuming food.

clue.text: In pay structure, money was advanced abundantly

indicators.note: In places the loan inside the rearranged letters
structure here means the letters are built into a new form

parts.note: money advanced to someone was lent

explanation.surface: Under the salary scheme, generous advances were made.
explanation.definitionFit: Means in great quantity, as in food in abundance.

clue.text: He set up the NHS in Britain yesteryear

indicators.note: in tells us the name is concealed within the following words

explanation.surface: A history fact about the founder of Britain's health service.
explanation.walkthrough: Aneurin 'Nye' Bevan was the Labour minister who founded the National Health Service in 1948.
explanation.definitionFit: Aneurin Bevan, known by this nickname, was the minister who created Britain's National Health Service.

clue.text: Make an effort to be delivered out of that temptation

indicators.note: delivered out of means the word is extracted from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A plea to be delivered from temptation, as in the Lord's Prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: To try at something is to put effort in.

clue.text: Exchanged for the racket that goes on in the Exchange

definitions.text: the racket that goes on in the Exchange

explanation.surface: Swapping something amid the noise of a stock exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as TRADE DIN: the noise (din) of dealing (trade).
explanation.definitionFit: Given in part payment for a new item, and also the clamour of dealing on a trading floor.

clue.text: Depending upon a current shade of blue

explanation.surface: A colour that relies on a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: Powered by electricity flowing through a wire, and also a vivid, bright steely blue colour.

clue.text: Maybe the secret of the bowler's success, but not on a motor outing

definitions.text: Maybe the secret of the bowler's success

parts.note: a switch not on is off
a spin is a short drive in a car

explanation.surface: A bowler's secret weapon, but not useful on a car trip.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, off-spin is a bowler's technique of turning the ball from the off side; 'bowler' looks like a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket bowling technique that turns the ball off the pitch and can take wickets.

clue.text: Apply by letter to remove bad debts from your books

definitions.text: remove bad debts from your books

explanation.surface: Advice on handling paperwork and accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: To send away for something by post, and to cancel an unrecoverable sum in accounts.

clue.text: Drum for the piper's son

explanation.surface: A drum belonging to a piper's boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom, Tom, the piper's son' is a nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall hand-beaten percussion instrument, and the nursery-rhyme boy who stole a pig.

clue.text: Elaborate on rate review

indicators.note: a review revises things, so the letters of the words are revised into a new order

explanation.surface: Expanding on a rate review.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate as an adjective means highly decorated, fussy in detail.

clue.text: Addled egg in a condition which suggests it is getting too old

indicators.note: addled means muddled or rotten, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A rotten egg is past its best.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing older, past one's prime.

clue.text: Loud advertisement creates a craze

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A noisy promotion sets off a craze.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-lived enthusiasm or vogue.

clue.text: A suit for a girl's best friend

explanation.surface: Something meant for a woman's dearest companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diamonds are a girl's best friend' is the famous song.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four sets in a pack of cards, and the gems a famous song calls a girl's best friend.

clue.text: Settle for ear, nose and throat then fall into bad health

parts.note: ENT is the hospital abbreviation for ear, nose and throat
to ail is to be unwell

explanation.surface: Accept a specialist referral before getting ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settle' is the legal sense: to settle property on a line of heirs.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, to bequeath an estate so it passes down a fixed line of heirs.

clue.text: A simple calculation suffices for a lot of diminutive soldiers

parts.note: a division is a large army unit of soldiers

explanation.surface: A small army unit is easy to count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' signals that a division is a large body of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Dividing by a small number done mentally without writing out the working.
